messages:
Marta: heads-up — ClipperAI asked for a latency guardrail on their high-qps embeddings flow, and wants a plan for any changes that could affect p95 within 2 weeks. they mentioned KV cache cold-starts as a big pain.
Kai: noted. do we have a quant/kv play that hits both latency and cost?
Anya: short answer: adaptive prefetching + predictive eviction helps p95, but adds memory pressure; quant helps cost but can regress quality for some emb models.
Jun: from infra side, adaptive prefetching is doable as an opt-in runtime flag. low-risk canary in dedicated pools.
Liam: is there telemetry we can ship quickly to prove impact? need p50/p95 tokens-per-request, cache hit rate, evictions/sec, memory headroom.
perf-bot: scheduled perf-canary job: kv-prefetch-canary on dedicated-qa starting 2050003000 (status: queued) :gear:
Marta: can we sketch launch criteria here so PM/sales can give ClipperAI a timeline? e.g., safety gates, perf targets, rollout plan.
Kai: proposal:
- Canary must show >=10% p95 reduction for their workload or no regressions for 3 days
- Cache hit rate improvement >=15% at steady state
- Memory overhead <8% on 48GB instance types
- Automated fallback to current behavior on OOM or >2x eviction spike
Anya: add quality guard: embedding cosine similarity drift <0.5% on a holdout set (Clipper provided sample).
Jun: rollout steps: opt-in canary (dedicated), subset of traffic with tight tracing, then A/B 10/90, then 50/50, then global. each step min 72h unless metrics stable for 24h and manual sign-off.
Marta: timeline? we have two weeks from Clipper to present plan. realistic earliest canary start is next Tues (2050003000).
Liam: who owns the experiment dashboard? I can wire up a per-route dashboard with the bins we need if someone exposes metrics.
Kai: I'll add runtime config: `kv.prefetch_mode=adaptive`, `kv.prefetch_lookahead=128`, `kv.max_prefetch_mem_pct=8`. quick patch to API surface and a feature flag.
Anya: note: for quant interplay — if model runs in 4-bit path, prefetching memory layout changes. compatibility test needed for LLMs with fused kernels.
Jun: add canary checklist item: validate kernel compatibility across forks (cuBlas/cuDNN/oneDNN) we use. if mismatch, auto-fallback.
Marta: decision needed: do we bundle quant-work in the same iteration or treat as follow-up? sales wants cost estimate now.
Kai: recommend split: land prefetch canary first (fast win for latency). parallelize quant experiments but don't gate Clipper rollout on quant.
Anya: agreed. quant experiments need new eval harness and regression alerts — estimate 3 sprints to be safe.
Liam: I'll produce an initial perf dashboard before canary start. tag me in the PR for metric names.
Marta: action items (owner -> ETA):
- Kai -> runtime flag + feature flag PR (ETA: 2050002000)
- Jun -> canary infra + auto-fallback (ETA: 2050002600)
- Liam -> dashboard wiring (ETA: 2050002800)
- Anya -> quality holdout + eval script (ETA: 2050002700)
- Marta -> customer-facing plan + timeline (ETA: 2050002900)
perf-bot: canary job started: kv-prefetch-canary on dedicated-qa at 2050003000 (status: running)
Kai: pinging @here — PR up, config flags are behind `runtime.experiments.kv_adaptive_prefetch`. rough cfg in the PR description.
Anya: quick note: add regression alert thresholds to the rollout policy (auto-rollback if similarity drift >0.8% or p95 regresses >3ms).
Jun: canary infra shows initial memory bump ~5% and hit rate +18% on synthetic trace. looks promising.
Liam: dashboard shows p95 down 12% for the sampled route, steady for 6hrs. will continue monitoring.
Marta: thanks team. we'll brief ClipperAI tomorrow with this phased plan. follow-ups: quant sequencing, pricing note if we can show unit cost delta after quant.
Kai: filing a small RFC for kernel-compat tests as a dependency for later quant items.
Anya: added notes to the eval repo about embedding drift checks and sample size.
Marta: closing loop — recording decisions: 1) proceed with adaptive prefetch canary now, 2) split quant into separate initiative, 3) strict quality gates required before any opt-in to quantized runtime. I'll drop summary to sales. :white_check_mark:
